question: Re-fetch Śatapatha III.2.1: verify ground/sitting skins versus the garment-attached horn and the footnote-mediated school difference; retain reversible white/black assignments and do not equate the skin term with the horn or claim first-hand Kanva Sanskrit.
source_locator: ŚB (Mādhyandina text, Eggeling trans., SBE 26) III,2,1 as hosted on the cited wisdomlib chapter page: §1 — two black antelope skins spread on the ground south of the Āhavanīya as image of the two worlds; §3 — one-skin option whose white/black world assignment is explicitly reversible ('or, if he likes, conversely'); §5, §8–9 — the officiant squats behind, kneels on, and sits down on the skins; §18 — 'he ties a black deer's horn to the end (of his garment)'; §28 — the horn is bound tightly to the garment end and skin vs horn receive distinct identifications (skin = the sacrifice, horn = the womb); §29 — tied with the open part upward like a womb; §31 — scratching only with the horn; footnote 9 (anchored to §18) — Mādhyandinas tied it to the unwoven end (thrum, daśā) of the nether garment, Kāṇvas to the hem of the upper garment (cf. Kāty. VII, 3, 29 scholl.); footnote 2 (anchored to §3) — Kāṇva colour variant quoted by Eggeling
source_excerpt: the black deer skin is the same as that sacrifice, and the black deer's horn is the same as that womb … therefore it (the horn) is bound tightly (to the end of the garment)
retrieval_method: FetchURL live round-7 re-fetch of the entry's cited wisdomlib chapter page (Eggeling translation, ŚB Kāṇḍa III, Adhyāya 2, Brāhmaṇa 1); full chapter §§ 1–40 with footnotes retrieved in one live call, not a search snippet; the excerpt above is taken fresh from this fetch, not copied from the round-6 ledger. Raw evidence copy (git-ignored): reports/supplement-opencode-1/scratch/round7-11-source-scribe/satapatha-3-2-1-refetch.md
basis: The question targets exactly this chapter and URL, and the live fetch returned §§ 1–40 plus footnotes, so every element is tested directly against retrieved text: §§ 1, 5, 8–9 show the skins as a ground/sitting surface (spread on the ground, squatted behind, knelt and sat on) — the sitting-surface reading survives this re-fetch; §§ 18, 28 show the horn as a worn garment-end attachment bound tightly, with §28 assigning skin and horn different identifications, so the two are textually distinct items; §3 states the white/black assignment is reversible in-text; footnote 9 records the Mādhyandina/Kāṇva attachment difference as Eggeling's footnote; footnote 2 quotes a Kāṇva colour variant. Nothing in the retrieved text equates the horn with the skin.
limits: Translation-mediated: Eggeling's English (1885) on wisdomlib hosting; the page advertises '[Sanskrit text for this chapter is available]' but only the English and footnotes were retrieved, so no Sanskrit and no first-hand Kāṇva recension were inspected — the Kāṇva readings (footnotes 2, 5, 9, 10, 12, 15, 16, incl. 'uttarasice!' inside footnote 9) are known only as quoted by Eggeling. 'black deer skin/horn' is the translator's rendering; the retrieved English page nowhere displays the lemma kṛṣṇājina, so identifying the skin term with kṛṣṇājina rests on prior scholarship, not this fetch, and the horn is not the skin term (§28 keeps them distinct). The §3 colour scheme is reversible in-text, so no fixed white=sky / black=earth convention is asserted. Footnote 9's school difference is translator-mediated (Kāty. VII, 3, 29 scholl. not independently inspected). One school's Soma-dīkṣā prescription: supports no pan-Vedic costume reconstruction and no universal dress law. Extraction artifacts preserved in the raw copy: footnote [18]'s body did not come through (list jumps [17]→[19]); 'oil earth' in §40 is as-extracted. Wisdomlib hosting can drift at any time; this is author-side evidence, not promotion verification.
coupling_implication: The S04 bridge stays scoped exactly as before: 'surface vs worn attachment' remain distinct slots — a spread ground surface is not a worn item, and the horn-like implement is a garment-end attachment with its own womb analogy and scratching function; colour symbolism enters only as an explicitly reversible assignment, never a fixed white/black key; any Mādhyandina-vs-Kāṇva comparison enters only as a translator-reported footnote variant, not first-hand recension evidence.

additional_excerpts.III,2,1,1: South of the Āhavanīya he spreads two black antelope skins on the ground, with the neck parts towards the east: thereon he consecrates him.
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,3 (reversible assignment clause): --or, if he likes, conversely: those which are black are an image of the sky, and those which are white are (an image) of this (earth).
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,5: He then squats down behind the two skins, with his face towards the east and with bent (right) knee
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,8: He then kneels down with his right knee (on the skin)
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,9: He must indeed sit down first on the hind part (of the skin).
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,18: Thereupon he ties a black deer's horn to the end (of his garment).
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,28 (binding clause): And because it was by pressing it tightly together that Indra tore out (the womb), therefore it (the horn) is bound tightly (to the end of the garment)
additional_excerpts.III,2,1,31: therefore the consecrated should scratch himself with the black deer's horn and with nothing but the black deer's horn
additional_excerpts.footnote_9: The Mādhyandinas tied the horn to the unwoven end (thrum, daśā) of the nether garment which was tucked through (par. 13) and then allowed to hang down in front. The Kāṇvas, on the other hand, tied it to the hem of the upper garment (uttarasice! Kāṇva text); cf. Kāty. VII, 3, 29 scholl.
additional_excerpts.footnote_2: Yāny eva babhrūṇiva harīṇi. The Kāṇva text reads, Yāny eva madhye babhrūṇi vā harīṇi vā, 'those in the centre (or between the black and white) which are either brown or yellow (grey).'
